title: Chapter 21: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

blocks.content: The Prime Minister is the head of the government in India and the most powerful political authority in the parliamentary system. While the President is the nominal executive head, the real executive powers are exercised by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The relevant constitutional provisions are mainly found in Articles 74 to 78 in Part V of the Constitution.
1. Constitutional Articles Related to Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Prime Minister serves as the real executive authority (de facto head), whereas the President is the nominal executive (de jure head).
According to Article 75, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
The Council of Ministers operates under the principle of Collective Responsibility to the Lok Sabha as specified in Article 75.
The Council of Ministers is a three-tiered body comprising Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
Article 78 defines the key duties of the Prime Minister as the chief channel of communication between the Cabinet and the President.

blocks.content: 2. Appointment of the Prime Minister
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India.
• Usually the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha is appointed as Prime Minister.
• If no party gets majority (hung parliament), the President may appoint the leader who can prove majority support in the Lok Sabha.
• Other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
3. Qualifications of the Prime Minister
• Must be a citizen of India.
• Must be a member of either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha).
• If a person is not a member at the time of appointment, he/she must become a member within six months.
4. Oath of Office and Secrecy
The Prime Minister takes oath of office and secrecy administered by the President of India according to the Third Schedule of the Constitution.
5. Structure of the Council of Ministers

blocks.content: The Cabinet is the core decision‑making body of the government and consists of the most senior ministers.
6. Powers and Functions of the Prime Minister
Executive Powers
• Head of the Council of Ministers.
• Advises the President regarding appointment of ministers.
• Advises appointment of Governors, judges, Attorney General, and other key officials.
• Coordinates activities of all ministries.
Legislative Powers
• Leader of the Lok Sabha (if member of Lok Sabha).
• Advises the President to summon and dissolve Lok Sabha.

blocks.content: • Plays a major role in the legislative agenda of the Parliament.
Administrative Powers
• Allocates portfolios among ministers.
• Reshuffles or removes ministers.
• Coordinates policies of different ministries.
Diplomatic Powers
• Represents India in international forums.
• Plays a key role in foreign policy decisions.
Emergency Role
• Advises the President regarding declaration of emergency.
• Leads the government during national crises.
7. Collective Responsibility

items: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha specifically, NOT to the Parliament as a whole.
A non-member of Parliament can be appointed as a Minister or Prime Minister, but must get elected to either House within 6 months.
The word 'Cabinet' was not originally in the Constitution; it was inserted in Article 352 by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.

blocks.content: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence against the government, the entire Council of Ministers including the Prime Minister must resign.
8. Cabinet vs Council of Ministers

cells: Larger body including all categories of ministers

blocks.content: EXAM Important Facts
• Articles 74–78 deal with Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.
• Prime Minister is the real executive authority in India.
• Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.
• First Prime Minister of India – Jawaharlal Nehru.
